checks.note: It names the mutable default argument `cart=[]` on the def line as the cause.
It says the list is created once at definition time, so every call without `cart` appends to the same list and the total keeps growing.
The fix uses `cart=None` with an `if cart is None: cart = []` guard, which is the standard fix.
Only the default value changes and a two-line guard is added. The rest of the function body is unchanged.
The explanation is accurate and short. The example outputs (2, 10, then 2, 12 with a shared cart) are correct. The closing 'Other problems' note is slightly extra but brief and correct.
